Taṇhāvagga 24. Craving The Craving Chapter

Kapilamacchavatthu

Manujassa pamattacārino, When a man lives heedlessly, For a person who lives negligently, Taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya; craving grows in them like a camel’s foot creeper. craving grows like vines; So plavatī hurā huraṁ, They jump from one thing to the next, like a langur they drift from life to life, Phalamicchaṁva vanasmi vānaro. greedy for fruit in a forest grove. like a monkey in the forest wishing for fruit.

Yaṁ esā sahate jammī, Whoever is beaten by this wretched craving, When one is overcome by that which is despicable - taṇhā loke visattikā; this attachment to the world, craving, which keeps us stuck in the world - Sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti, their sorrow grows, then sorrow grows in them, abhivaṭṭhaṁva bīraṇaṁ. like grass in the rain. like weeds after rain.

Yo cetaṁ sahate jammiṁ, But whoever prevails over this wretched craving, When one overcomes that which is despicable - taṇhaṁ loke duraccayaṁ; so hard to get over in the world, craving, which is so hard to transcend in this world - Sokā tamhā papatanti, their sorrows fall from them, then sorrow falls away from them, udabinduva pokkharā. like a drop from a lotus-leaf. like drops of water from a lotus.

Taṁ vo vadāmi bhaddaṁ vo, I say this to you, good people, I wish the best to all of you yāvantettha samāgatā; all those who have gathered here: that are gathered here - Taṇhāya mūlaṁ khaṇatha, dig up the root of craving, dig up the root of craving, usīratthova bīraṇaṁ; as you’d dig up grass in search of roots. as one seeks the root of a weed; Mā vo naḷaṁva sotova, Don’t let Māra break you again and again, do not let Māra subdue you again and again, māro bhañji punappunaṁ. like a stream breaking a reed. like a stream does to reeds.

Sūkarapotikāvatthu

Yathāpi mūle anupaddave daḷhe, A tree grows back even when cut down, As long as its root is undisturbed and strong, Chinnopi rukkho punareva rūhati; so long as its roots are strong and undamaged; a felled tree grows again. Evampi taṇhānusaye anūhate, suffering springs up again and again, In the same way, as long as the tendency towards craving is not destroyed, Nibbattatī dukkhamidaṁ punappunaṁ. so long as the tendency to craving is not pulled out. it produces suffering again and again.

Yassa chattiṁsati sotā, A person of low views If the 36 streams manāpasavanā bhusā; in whom the thirty-six streams are flowing strongly towards what one likes, Mahāvahanti duddiṭṭhiṁ, that flow to pleasure are mighty, then one is swept along by harmful views saṅkappā rāganissitā. is swept away by lustful thoughts. and attitudes based on passion.

Savanti sabbadhi sotā, The streams flow everywhere; Streams flow everywhere, latā uppajja tiṭṭhati; a weed springs up and remains. creepers appear and remain; Tañca disvā lataṁ jātaṁ, Seeing this weed that has been born, having seen the birth of the creeper, mūlaṁ paññāya chindatha. cut the root with wisdom. cut its root with wisdom.

Saritāni sinehitāni ca, A personage’s joys Currents of infatuation Somanassāni bhavanti jantuno; flow from senses and cravings. and elation exist in people; Te sātasitā sukhesino, Seekers of happiness, bent on pleasure, those who are addicted to comfort, seeking pleasure, Te ve jātijarūpagā narā. continue to be reborn and grow old. arrive at rebirth and decrepitude.

Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā, People governed by thirst, Pursued by craving, Parisappanti sasova bandhito; crawl about like a trapped rabbit. people thrash about like a trapped rabbit; Saṁyojanasaṅgasattakā, Bound and fettered, for a long time bound by attachment and adherence, Dukkhamupenti punappunaṁ cirāya. they return to pain time and again. they come to suffering again and again for a long time.

Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā, People governed by thirst, Pursued by craving, Parisappanti sasova bandhito; crawl about like a trapped rabbit. people thrash about like a trapped rabbit; Tasmā tasiṇaṁ vinodaye, That’s why one who longs for dispassion therefore, one should remove craving, Ākaṅkhanta virāgamattano. should dispel thirst. wishing to be dispassionate.

Vibbhantabhikkhuvatthu

Yo nibbanatho vanādhimutto, Unsnarled, they set out for the jungle, One who has left the forest yet is intent upon the forest, Vanamutto vanameva dhāvati; then they run right back to the jungle they left behind. though free from the forest, runs back to the forest. Taṁ puggalametha passatha, Just look at this individual! Look at that person; Mutto bandhanameva dhāvati. Freed, they run to bondage. although free, they run back to imprisonment.

Bandhanāgāravatthu

Na taṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā, The attentive say that shackle is not strong The wise say that prisons Yadāyasaṁ dārujapabbajañca; that’s made of iron, wood, or knots. made of iron, wood, and thatch Sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu, But obsession with jeweled earrings, are not as strong as Puttesu dāresu ca yā apekkhā. concern for your partners and children: obsession with jewelry, children, and spouses.

Etaṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā, this, say the attentive, is a strong shackle The wise say that this is a strong prison Ohārinaṁ sithilaṁ duppamuñcaṁ; dragging the indulgent down, hard to escape. which oppresses the lax and is hard to escape from. Etampi chetvāna paribbajanti, Having cut this one too they go forth, They break free and become renunciants, Anapekkhino kāmasukhaṁ pahāya. unconcerned, having given up sensual pleasures. leaving behind sensual pleasure without looking back.

Khemātherīvatthu

Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṁ, Besotted by lust they fall into the stream, Those who fall into the stream of passion Sayaṅkataṁ makkaṭakova jālaṁ; like a spider caught in the web she wove. are like a spider stuck in its own web. Etampi chetvāna vajanti dhīrā, The attentive proceed, having cut this one too, The wise break free and move on, Anapekkhino sabbadukkhaṁ pahāya. unconcerned, having given up all suffering. leaving behind all suffering without looking back.

Uggasenavatthu

Muñca pure muñca pacchato, Let go of the past, let go of the future, Be free before, be free after, Majjhe muñca bhavassa pāragū; let go of the present, having gone beyond rebirth. be free in the middle; transcend existence. Sabbattha vimuttamānaso, With your heart freed in every respect, With a mind liberated everywhere, Na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi. you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age. do not return again to birth and decrepitude.

Cūḷadhanuggahapaṇḍitavatthu

Vitakkamathitassa jantuno, For a personage churned by thoughts, When one has disturbed thoughts, Tibbarāgassa subhānupassino; very lustful, focusing on beauty, strong passion, and fixation on beauty, Bhiyyo taṇhā pavaḍḍhati, their craving grows and grows, then craving grows ever greater Esa kho daḷhaṁ karoti bandhanaṁ. tying them with a stout bond. and makes a strong prison.

Vitakkūpasame ca yo rato, But one who loves to calm their thoughts, One who approves of tranquil thought, Asubhaṁ bhāvayate sadā sato; developing perception of ugliness, ever mindful, who has cultivated awareness of non-beauty and is always mindful, Esa kho byanti kāhiti, will surely eliminate that craving, will put an end to that craving Esa checchati mārabandhanaṁ. cutting off the bonds of Māra. and break free of Māra’s prison.

Māravatthu

Niṭṭhaṅgato asantāsī, One who is confident, unafraid, When one has reached the final destination, is fearless, vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo; rid of craving, free of blemish, free of craving, flawless, Acchindi bhavasallāni, having struck down the arrows flying to future lives, and has broken the thorn of existence, antimoyaṁ samussayo. this bag of bones is their last. then they bear their last body.

Vītataṇho anādāno, Rid of craving, free of grasping, When one is free of craving, not acquisitive, Niruttipadakovido; expert in the definition of terms, and is a master of words and phrases Akkharānaṁ sannipātaṁ, knowing the correct who knows the proper grouping Jaññā pubbāparāni ca; structure and sequence of syllables, and sequencing of sentences, Sa ve “antimasārīro, they are said to be one who bears their final body, then they are called a bearer of their last body, Mahāpañño mahāpuriso”ti vuccati. one of great wisdom, a great person. a great person of great wisdom.

Upakājīvakavatthu

Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūhamasmi, I am the vanquisher of all, the knower of all, I have overcome all, I know all; Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto; unsullied in the midst of all things. amidst all things I am unsullied; Sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto, I’ve given up all, freed in the ending of craving. I have relinquished everything and I am liberated through the elimination of craving - Sayaṁ abhiññāya kamuddiseyyaṁ. Since I know for myself, whose follower should I be? knowing this directly and personally, who could I indicate as my teacher?

Sakkapañhavatthu

Sabbadānaṁ dhammadānaṁ jināti, The gift of the teaching surmounts all other gifts; The gift of Dhamma trumps all gifts, Sabbarasaṁ dhammaraso jināti; the taste of the teaching surmounts all other tastes; the taste of Dhamma trumps all tastes, Sabbaratiṁ dhammarati jināti, the joy of the teaching surmounts all other joys; the appreciation of Dhamma trumps all appreciation, Taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṁ jināti. the ending of craving surmounts all suffering. the elimination of craving trumps all suffering.

Aputtakaseṭṭhivatthu

Hananti bhogā dummedhaṁ, Riches ruin a simpleton, Wealth destroys a fool no ca pāragavesino; but not a seeker of the far shore. who does not seek transcendence; Bhogataṇhāya dummedho, From craving for wealth, a simpleton a fool who craves wealth hanti aññeva attanaṁ. ruins themselves and others. harms both self and others.

Aṅkuravatthu

Tiṇadosāni khettāni, Weeds are the bane of crops, Grass is the defect of fields, rāgadosā ayaṁ pajā; but greed is these folk’s bane. passion is the defect of this generation; Tasmā hi vītarāgesu, That’s why a gift to one rid of greed therefore a gift given to those free of passion dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ. is so very fruitful. is of great benefit.

Tiṇadosāni khettāni, Weeds are the bane of crops, Grass is the defect of fields, dosadosā ayaṁ pajā; but hate is these folk’s bane. hatred is the defect of this generation; Tasmā hi vītadosesu, That’s why a gift to one rid of hate therefore a gift given to those free of hate dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ. is so very fruitful. is of great benefit.

Tiṇadosāni khettāni, Weeds are the bane of crops, Grass is the defect of fields, mohadosā ayaṁ pajā; but delusion is these folk’s bane. delusion is the defect of this generation; Tasmā hi vītamohesu, That’s why a gift to one rid of delusion therefore a gift given to those free of delusion dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ. is so very fruitful. is of great benefit.

Tiṇadosāni khettāni, Weeds are the bane of crops, Grass is the defect of fields, icchādosā ayaṁ pajā; but desire is these folk’s bane. craving is the defect of this generation; Tasmā hi vigaticchesu, That’s why a gift to one rid of desire therefore a gift given to those free of craving dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ. is so very fruitful. is of great benefit.

Taṇhāvaggo catuvīsatimo.
